controlDescription: Inactive system accounts must be automatically disabled within 30 days for High-Confidentiality/High-Integrity systems (standard NIST default is 90 days).
controlSupplementalText: Account management procedures for NSS must account for personnel security clearances and formal access authorizations (e.g., need-to-know determinations). System accounts associated with personnel whose clearance or access authorization has been revoked must be terminated immediately (within 24 hours).

controlDescription: Access control mechanisms must enforce explicit security attributes, including security classification markings, handling caveats, and compartment designations.
controlSupplementalText: For NSS processing classified national security information (CNSI), logical access enforcement must prevent lower-cleared or non-compartmented users from viewing, querying, or executing data tagged with higher security attributes or specific dissemination controls (e.g., NOFORN, PROPIN).

controlDescription: Non-privileged users must be strictly prohibited from executing system utilities or administrative applications that bypass auditing or access controls.
controlSupplementalText: In NSS environments, dual-authorization (two-person control) must be implemented for critical administrative functions, such as modifying system security configurations, changing cryptographic keys, or wiping audit logs.

controlDescription: Remote access to NSS from non-NSS perimeters is prohibited unless protected by NSA-approved Cryptographic High Assurance (Type 1) mechanisms or an Authorizing Official (AO)-approved enclave perimeter.
controlSupplementalText: Unencrypted remote access, dial-up access, or split-tunneling on remote devices connected to NSS is explicitly forbidden. Wireless remote access must comply with specific CNSS wireless instructions (CNSSI 7003 / CNSSAM TEMPEST).

controlDescription: Audit logging capabilities cannot be disabled or altered by privileged system accounts without triggering an immediate high-priority security alert.
controlSupplementalText: CNSSI 1253 establishes mandatory non-tailorable audit logging requirements for NSS. Auditable events must include all privilege escalations, cross-domain file transfers, cryptographic operations, failed logon attempts, and modifications to access control lists.

controlDescription: Audit records must be reviewed at least weekly using automated log analysis and correlation tools.
controlSupplementalText: Automated analysis must look for cross-boundary leakages, unauthorized access attempts to classified repositories, and insider threat anomalies. Real-time alerts must be routed directly to the Information System Security Manager (ISSM) or Security Operations Center (SOC).

controlDescription: Audit logs must be retained online for a minimum of 90 days and archived offline for a minimum of 5 years (or per agency-specific national security record schedules).
controlSupplementalText: Archived logs must be cryptographically protected against tampering or unauthorized deletion to preserve evidentiary chain-of-custody for national security investigations.

controlDescription: Hardware-based multi-factor authentication (MFA) utilizing National Security System-approved PKI certificates or DoD Common Access Cards (CAC) / Personal Identity Verification (PIV) tokens is mandatory for all access.
controlSupplementalText: Passwords alone are not authorized for primary authentication on NSS. Remote and local administrative logins require hardware-based cryptographic credentials.

controlDescription: Passwords used as secondary authenticators or for local recovery accounts must be a minimum of 15 characters for general users and 20 characters for privileged accounts.
controlSupplementalText: Authenticators must be changed every 60 days and cannot reuse the previous 24 passwords. System authenticators must be stored using approved cryptographic hashes (e.g., FIPS-validated / NSA-approved hashing algorithms).

controlDescription: Removable media (e.g., flash drives, external hard drives, optical discs) must be physically marked with the highest classification level and caveats of the information stored or processed on the system.
controlSupplementalText: Unapproved commercial USB flash drives are strictly prohibited on NSS. Hardware perimeters must physically or logically disable unauthorized USB mass storage devices.

controlDescription: Media sanitization and destruction must strictly comply with NSA/CSS Policy Manual 9-12 or NSA-approved sanitization evaluators (EPLs).
controlSupplementalText: Standard software overwrites or commercial formatting are insufficient for classified National Security Systems media. Physical destruction (incineration, shredding to NSA particle size, or degaussing via an NSA-approved degausser) is required and must be witnessed by two cleared individuals.

controlDescription: Systems processing classified NSS data must reside within accredited physical perimeters, such as Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs) or designated secure rooms complying with CNSS specifications.
controlSupplementalText: Physical security perimeters must incorporate Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS), acoustic protection, physical access logs, and TEMPEST emission security measures (CNSSAM TEMPEST/1-13) to prevent emanations tapping.

controlDescription: Interconnections between NSS and non-NSS (or between different security classification levels) must be managed through an AO-approved Guard or Cross Domain Solution (CDS).
controlSupplementalText: Direct, unmonitored routing between networks of different classification levels or security domains is prohibited. Cross Domain Solutions must be tested and certified in accordance with NSA/CDMO guidelines.

controlDescription: Cryptographic mechanisms protecting classified national security data in transit or at rest must utilize NSA-approved Type 1 Cryptography or Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) architectures.
controlSupplementalText: Standard commercial FIPS 140-2/140-3 validation alone is insufficient for protecting classified national security data across unapproved perimeters. Data in transit across unclassified networks must be encapsulated in NSA-certified Type 1 encryptors (e.g., HAIPE).

controlDescription: Cryptographic mechanisms protecting classified national security data in transit or at rest must utilize NSA-approved Type 1 Cryptography or Commercial Solutions for Classified (CSfC) architectures.
controlSupplementalText: Standard commercial FIPS 140-2/140-3 validation alone is insufficient for protecting classified national security data across unapproved perimeters. Data in transit across unclassified networks must be encapsulated in NSA-certified Type 1 encryptors (e.g., HAIPE).

controlDescription: Intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS) must be deployed at all internal and external perimeters, specifically configured to monitor for indicators of insider threat and nation-state threat activity.
controlSupplementalText: Continuous monitoring tools must feed security event data into centralized defense-wide or agency-wide SOC architectures (e.g., US-CERT / DoD Cyber Command reporting mechanisms).
